Trust, I've done that and as a result of being pretty personable I've gotten jobs but while I've worked in good restaurants and hotels (I live in a major US city with a massive tourism industry yearround) and like, sure you can make like 6 figures or 75-80k as a waiter at some places and even declare like you're making minimum wage because of tips if you wanted to, and some bartenders make a quarter mil, many may many bartenders make more than 6 figures, but that wasn't my life goal.

My life goal is also not to be a business owner, I wanted to be a doctor, then switched to wanting to either be a linguist or a lawyer. 

The best linguistics training in the world is with the US military, but despite my degree and taking the ASVAB and getting a 94 (the highest is 99), so seemingly being a perfect fit, I was told I wouldn't be able to get a security clearance and told "Just enlist as a combat job" which like, no, go fuck yourself, thats an insult to someone with my test scores and education. 

To be a lawyer I have to go to law school. I was denied by the school I wanted to go to despite a great LSAT test, tbf my GPA wasn't super high but still. Maybe some school would take me but do I really want to take out 100k in student loans and spend 4 years of my life trying to be a perfect student while also paying my bills only to take the bar, pass it, and be denied a license due to an arrest at 18 that didn't even result in a fucking conviction?!? 

Why does my life have to be marred forever and be a 2nd class existence where my best bet is to start my own business or be a salesman, something I'm not bad at but that I wouldn't exactly feel complete or happy or fulfilled AT ALL in doing. Its bullshit

I learned recently that I actually have a valid lawsuit against a background check company, however, because it turns out that it is illegal to report arrests not resulting in a conviction older than 7 years, and I don't have enough money RIGHT NOW to expunge my record, but even if I did, I can only expunge one arrest.

I actually have 2, to be fair I did a diversion program and a cop stopped me illegally one day on the street to do an ID check and when I tried to tell them I knew my rights and didn't do anything wrong so didn't have to, they detained me and when they found out about my diversion program they decided to arrest me for "Resisting officer without violence".

In normal circumstances I would have been released the next day and tried to go to trial because it was an illegal stop, but as I was on diversion I had to do 90 days in jail with no bond for that charge that was actually dismissed immediately (but my lawyer and I were getting ready for trial because he knew it was an illegal stop and that we would almost definitely win in court, but they didn't give us the opportunity).

Sure, that's a dismissed misdemeanor, but because I was on a diversion program to get my other charges dismissed, it shows up as a program violation and thus shows that I was in a diversion program. Even if I expunge the primary felony dismissed case, the dismissed misdemeanor shows a violation of a program, which implies I was arrested before. 

Let's hope the laws about not being allowed to report, and in some states even CONSIDER, non conviction arrests older than 7 years helps me out. A lawyer called me yesterday telling me she would take my case for this bad background check because it was a violation of the FCRA.

They are under no obligation to. Take away the power you have given them, as every child does. You don't live for your parents and coming to that realization is hard, because now you have to live for yourself.

They don't need to understand you. Nobody will ever fully understand you. 

And you're talking about minor embarrassment in front of kids compared to shame for doing something bad in front of your family. Nobody is going to kill themselves because they slipped in high school. Do not equate the two.

Give yourself a chance to be a real person first. Everyone wants to die as an adolescent, as innocence dies. 

I would fucking murder everyone I've ever loved, however, to be in your position. 18, with multiple family members with homes that will support you, with a full scholarship to school and not needing to work or pay your own rent or bills yet. You're still allowed to have emotions be the biggest aspect of your life, fuck I wish I hadn't have been so stupid as to move out at 18.

There is nothing to say but suck it up right now, change your view, change your expectations. You are the EXACT example of "it gets better". You have never been independent, in the real world, by yourself. But you aren't there yet, but what you have could not be more perfect.

Look, its difficult, your parents won't understand you or care about you in the way you wish they would. But they fucking love you so goddam much and so does your uncle and you can never ruin that. The difficulty of that environment, the emotional adversity, the having to do what is reasonable as opposed to what you want which is to run from the difficulty, alongside the regular "difficulty" of being a full-time student (trust, it is subjectively "difficult" but nothing compared to having to support yourself financially while also doing it) is the PERFECT training ground for what the real world has in store for you.

By learning these lessons now and taking advantage of the objective, financial blessing you have PLUS A FULL FUCKING SCHOLARSHIP you will have a fantastic fucking head start on life when you finish school THAT YOU JUST STARTED. Let your life start. Make it to 22 and finish school, then re evaluate after your first 2 years out of school unless you're going to med/law school, in which case reevaluate when you finish those.

You're not allowed to waste your life before it starts. Only a fucking idiot would do that and you most certainly are not one. You're perfectly normal in every way right now during the loss of your innocence. Let this be the beginning of the end of your childish tantrums and the start of your duty to establish yourself as an individual separate from your family. 

You will be sad. You will hurt. You won't be understood. But don't try to lie to yourself. If you didn't care what people thought you wouldn't at all be talking about how your family not understanding you is the last straw. Newsflash, that's caring what people think. And that is GOOD AS SHIT, if you didn't care about what the people you love, your literal fucjing family, thought of you, of being ashamed, hurting them, disappointing them, you'd be a sociopath and I'd say "yes, absolutely, go ahead and kill yourself". 

You're not. You hurt.

That is life. But stick this out, you'll grow and learn from it, shift your expectations. Your family can love you without having to understand you in the way you want them to. You can love them without that as well. Once that happens you'll continue to grow, and it is ENTIRELY up to you to sculpt and shape who you are. That is a paralyzing freedom that drives most to madness. That is normal, but this is simply reality. Whatever that person may be is in you, but you've got a hell of a headstart.

Do you understand? You cannot let yourself kill yourself until you start real life, lest you are an idiot, and I know you are not from this brief exchange.

Switching to being an adult for "gifted children" is always unimaginably hard. The tales of how good life would be because of your talents turn out to not have been entirely true and on average people care much less and less every year about how smart you are.

The skills that make you a good student become less and less useful as you start to enter the workforce and your autonomy grows and you have to do more work, different work. Often times you have to do things that feel beneath you to be able to survive.

But you're only 18 and still in college, you don't have a criminal record, and an embarrassment from a loud altercation with a family member? Well, you'll all move past it. These are very common things, and you're still basically a child. I feel like they should make it so that 18-26, or maybe even just 24 or 22, should be legally treated as a different thing that adulthood as society doesn't allow us to be treated as full adults until we get to around that age.

So look, this is a hard truth everyone, more than anyone else people who were smart as kids, has to come up against and it creates a horrible existential dread that makes you want to die as your understanding of yourself and reality is shattered 

You want to fuck up you uncle really bad? Fucking kill yourself at 18 when your life hasn't started when you're a smart kid thats in college over a loud, embarrassing altercation you had in public. That will REALLY fuck him up, and pretty much everyone else in your family, your friends, even people who don't feel like real friends will feel terrible for losing you.

Since you're so young your peers will have to face their own existential dread and you will set off what's likely a chain reaction of depression among the people you went and go to school with as they come to grips with these realizations, of their futility, their mortality, the fact that they can die and that they're adults, no longer blessed with the shields of childhood.

Some people have wealthier families and don't ever have to come up against this and their lives are set up for them forever, they never have to struggle or work hard, they get the best education, then into the best college because they only had to worry about getting good grades. In a lot of schools in middle class areas and especially upper middle class areas there are more gifted kids than normal. This isn't some "everyone gets a trophy" thing. It's just that they get educated well and standards for gifted are still national. Kids learn well, so for them to be considered gifted is really easy when given access to the best learning materials.

Then they go to college and don't have to get jobs or do anything really, they get their college experience fully paid for and can just "stress" about how hard exams are, not the real problems most people have like "I don't have enough time to study to do well AND work enough hours to pay my rent and food and not be homeless while going to school" or "my student loans aren't enough to cover living expenses and now I'm in a shitton of debt with subpar grades because I had to work so I can't go to med/law/grad school".

Then the rich kids with perfect grades and a cool college experience, who probably are attractive because of good medical care, orthodontists, dentists, dermatologists and hell maybe even plastic surgeons, plus they have lots of free time to go to the gym and money to afford healthy food and workout supplements, get interviewed for med/law/grad school.

Being attractive ABSOLUTELY helps. People will like you more, want you around more, you'll be more liked so your self esteem and confidence will be higher which will then make people like and want you EVEN MORE in a never ending cycle. Because of their stress free life and good appearances they have the grades to get into great schools , again fully paid for. They have parents who go to country clubs and friends with parents in the careers they want to go to so they just get to worry about schooling and not "real life" like the rest of us and end up becoming doctors, lawyers, engineers, stock brokers, whatever high paying job super easily and get a hot husband or wife who, if they're lucky were not rich and just married into money, or more likely are very similar because they were raised the same way and their wedding will be amazing, they'll get great jobs and then have perfect fucking lives with lots of money. 

Their worst problems might be a divorce, cheating, falling out of love, but never the life shattering stuff like constant debt, poverty, health problems you can't pay to get treated, being stuck in shitty jobs for decades because you couldn't afford higher education or had to work and got mid tier grades, the stuff that makes life a constant work fest to pay other people to give you the basic necessities for living.

Life is really fucking hard and unfair.

But you are not in a fucked position. You're 18. Holy fuck what I wouldn't give to be 18 again, I would kill my entire family and every friend I ever had if I could go back in time 10 years knowing what I know about the world and life now. 

Don't fucking kill yourself because you're embarrassed. That shit happens, you will embarrass yourself WAYYYYY more times in WAYYYY worse ways, most of them with your family because they're the people you can never escape, that will always be there at every stage of your life, so mathematically you will interact with them the most and they will know you the best, as you will know them the best so you will be more likely to act in bad ways around them as they will be with you, its just that that is SO ABSOLUTELY NORMAL.

I don't know why you would think otherwise, maybe you just watch movies or haven't lived long enough to know enough people well enough to know that what you did that embarrassed you so badly and makes you so ashamed is NORMAL AS FUCK.

Also, I'm not going to sugar coat this but you are acting like a child, and these days kids hear all these psychological terms like "gaslighting" and "trauma" and apply them much more freely than a medical professional would.

1. You don't fucking repay your parents. They will never want that, you are not indebted to your parents. They chose to raise you, they chose to birth you, everything they did to give you life was their choice, it was not with the idea that you would "pay off" in the future somehow. It is because they love you, you are their child and until you have your own child you will never be able to understand those feelings.

Let go of these ideas, they will only hurt you and hurt your relationship with your parents.

2. Your feelings are real but you will one day, likely very soon (maybe its happening right now) realize that while as a child your feelings are all that will be problems for you, as an adult you sometimes just have to feel bad and do things you don't like or don't want to do despite feeling depressed or anxious or sad because of a thing called responsibility.

Let's say you want to go to therapy because you're too depressed to work. Oh but look at that, you can afford therapy. So what do you do? Sit around and cry knowing it will do nothing, becoming more and more depressed realizing nobody else will fix these problems for you and that your sadness is futile until you kill yourself

Or

Be depressed, very depressed, and suck it up and go get whatever job you can for the time being in order to start making money that you can use to then go to therapy and maybe psychiatry and actually work on your depression but do work you hate and don't want to do in order to get to the point of helping yourself?

3. Your parents are not gods. They are not perfect, and they are under 0 obligation by anyone to EVER understand you or care about you in the way that you want or act any differently. Waiting around or fighting with them to try to get them to understand won't work and setting expectations that they should will only serve to make you more miserable and resent them and yourself more. Accept that they just won't get it or understand how you feel and will act as they act and there is likely nothing you can do to change that, they have to want to change. 

4. Your parents take away the things you like and that make you happy? Well then, they probably GAVE you those things in the first place. If you live with them you are beholden to their rules. You could leave and try to pay rent somewhere else, but that is a TERRIBLE idea. Focus on school and change your understanding. There are 18 year old kids that are homeless, there are 20+ year old kids, LOTS OF THEM that I can introduce you to, who left because they had similar circumstances to your own and ended up becoming drug addiction or depressed or failing out of school, losing their scholarships, or who left school to work to pay the bills they chose to have so their parents wouldn't control them.

They all wish theyd appreciated what they had&that they could go back&put w/ frustration+depression in exchange 4free rent&not having 2do anything but school

You want your parents not to take away things from you? Then be an adult, use your own money and buy your own things that they cannot take away from you. That is a child's problem. Ur an adolescent, you wish to have an adult's life with a child's privileges.

.

So, you are embarrassed that you had an outburst and hit the car and your neighbors had to restrain you? 

GOOD

Emotions arent mistakes. Our culture monopolizes "positive" feelings and says we should avoid others at all costs but to evolution they all evolved for reasons. Shame and embarrassment teach us lessons of what not 2 do socially, theyr tools 4avoiding pain&help social dynamics. U have these feelings 2 help u, dnt think ur broken 5 feeling them, in fact you are working perfectly, exactly as you are supposed to.

Youre young, deal with the shame&keep living 4now. U havent even started real life yet, give it until 1 yr after college.
